sections.heading: Verbs that need a preposition
sections.body: Many Spanish verbs require a specific preposition, often different from English. Learn them as units:

head: Preposition
Verbs
rows: *aprender a, empezar a, ayudar a, atreverse a* (to dare), *acostumbrarse a* (to get used to), *negarse a, invitar a, oler a* (to smell of), *saber a* (to taste of)
*depender de, acordarse de, olvidarse de, tratar de* (to try to), *enamorarse de, quejarse de, darse cuenta de* (to realize), *dejar de, cansarse de, burlarse de* (to make fun of)
*pensar en* (to think about), *confiar en, insistir en, tardar en, consistir en* (to consist of), *fijarse en* (to notice), *quedar en* (to agree to), *convertirse en*
*soñar con* (to dream of), *casarse con, contar con* (to count on), *encontrarse con* (to run into), *meterse con* (to pick on)
*preocuparse por* (to worry about), *interesarse por, luchar por, votar por, optar por* (to opt for)

sections.heading: The preposition stays with a clause
sections.body: When the verb is followed by *que* + clause, the preposition stays: *Me di cuenta de que era tarde.* (I realized it was late.) *Insisto en que vengas.* *Confío en que todo salga bien.* Dropping the *de* (*queísmo*: "me di cuenta que") is a common error in careful writing. *Dequeísmo* is the opposite error — adding *de* where it doesn't belong, as in "pienso de que": avoid it.

sections.heading: Pensar en vs. pensar de
sections.body: *Pensar en* = to think about (have in mind): *Pienso en ti.* *Pensar de* = to think of (opinion), usually in questions: *¿Qué piensas de la película?*

examples: Todo depende de ti.
Everything depends on you.
Trato de hablar español todos los días.
I try to speak Spanish every day.
Me di cuenta de que era tarde.
I realized it was late.
No me atrevo a decírselo.
I don't dare tell him.
Ya me acostumbré a vivir sola.
I've gotten used to living alone.
La cocina huele a café.
The kitchen smells of coffee.
Pienso en ti todos los días.
I think about you every day.
¿Qué piensas de la película?
What do you think of the movie?
El trabajo consiste en atender a los clientes.
The job consists of attending to customers.
¿Te fijaste en su vestido?
Did you notice her dress?
Sueño con viajar por Sudamérica.
I dream of traveling around South America.
Puedes contar conmigo.
You can count on me.
Me encontré con Pedro en el mercado.
I ran into Pedro at the market.
Se preocupa mucho por su hijo.
She worries a lot about her son.
No te burles de mí.
Don't make fun of me.
Me cansé de esperar.
I got tired of waiting.
Confío en que todo salga bien.
I trust everything will turn out well.
